findings.reason: a node told to implement exactly as written reaches a function that cannot compute the check it was given and must either pour disk access into the pure op validator or deviate, and the plan should name `_apply_evidence_appends`.
findings.text: the refusal is placed "beside its anchor-shape guard (`reckon/_store.py` near lines 1292–1299)" inside `_apply_append_evidence`, but that handler runs under `apply_ops`, whose contract is "Pure: never touches disk"; one of the three inputs the refusal needs — every id `_section_key` makes of the current ledger runs' `section` keys — is readable only from `ledger.runs(project, root=..., plan=...)`, which `_apply_append_evidence(working, op, is_index, warnings)` has no way to reach (no docs_dir, no root, no docs_dir/root anywhere; the impure half is `_apply_evidence_appends` at `reckon/_store.py:1230`, which does take them)

findings.reason: the plan's stated guarantee is a property of the operator-visible surface, and the surface that would carry it is out of the node's declared scope, so the node would deliver a field only a test reads.
findings.text: the deliverable accepts the residual collision because "it is never silent: when the rendered-id exclusion drops an appended section, the synthesis names it in its result", but the only production caller, `synthesize_evidence` (`reckon/project_maintenance_commands.py:1473-1485`), echoes just path, run count, comment count and commit count, and `EvidenceSynthesisResult` (`reckon/evidence.py:24-31`) has no field for a dropped name; that module is not among §4's write paths, so on the real code path the loss stays silent
